title: The three inputs
summary: Registrations come from LDAP (what a service means for a group of nodes) or the emergency services.txt and carry service, class, hook, protection and allowed principals; xtpd admits the service, loads its keys and records its hook. Service requests come from a local client on /run/xtpd.sock and carry service, peer and an optional client principal; xtpd opens the session and passes back a connected descriptor. Peerages come through the xtp.provision admission gate or the emergency peers.txt and carry peer, routes, keys and fence; xtpd installs routes and keys and adds the peer address to the nft set xtp_peers.
authority: design (architecture Tom Dyer; written by Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: Everything reaches xtpd as a registration, a service request or a peerage
Everything leaves as a hook, a firewall change or a receipt
procedure: Register a service; do not open a listener in the application

provenance.claim: xtp.provision ingress gate only; no actuator or identity resolver
Per-service keys, LDAP first then a mode-600 key file; protected FIRST checked before any state

qualification_boundaries.status: dev1 built: packages/oorexx_xtpd_v0.1-dev1 (Claude (Opus 5.5), 24 Nov 2026) - registrations, peerages and keys from files, unix-socket OPEN with descriptor passing, exec hooks, the fence, receipts through oorexx_logging
qualification_boundaries.field: tested on loopback only (two daemons, real OpenSSH over UDP and raw IP 36); not field-tested; LDAP inputs, operating states, emergency files and the role bootstrap are not built
